p001-u004: RoboMaster University Series Rule-Change Preview Manual
p002-u001: The RoboMaster Organizing Committee (RMOC) encourages and advocates technical innovation and open-source technology, and respects the intellectual property of participating teams. All intellectual property developed by a team during the competition belongs to that team. RMOC does not take part in resolving intellectual property disputes among team members. Teams must properly handle ownership relationships among their school members, company members, and members of other affiliations.
p002-u002: When using the Referee System and competition support materials provided by RMOC, teams must respect the intellectual property rights of the original product owners and must not reverse engineer, copy, translate, or otherwise act in any way that harms those owners' intellectual property rights.
p002-u003: For any act that infringes the intellectual property of competition education products provided by RMOC and the host organizations, the rights holder will pursue legal liability in accordance with the law.
p002-u004: For suggestions on open-source materials, see: https://bbs.robomaster.com/article/4820
p002-u006: The RoboMaster competition is a robot competition whose purpose is to cultivate young engineering talent. Related documents may include sensitive wording, names, operations, technologies, or other content. Such content does not reflect any technology or action existing in reality and is not intended to refer to any specific country, organization, or individual. This manual explains the robot competition rules and must not be used for any purpose other than the RoboMaster competition or be regarded as related to any real event or entity.
p006-u001: This chapter briefly describes the main rule adjustments for the RM2027 season. Compared with RM2026, the main revisions are as follows:
p006-u004: Redesigned the Aerial Robot's deployment, use, and functions.
p006-u006: The former Hero Robot and Engineer Robot are merged into the Heavy Robot.
p006-u008: The former Custom Controller and Custom Client are merged into the Custom Terminal.
p006-u011: The former Launch Ramp is replaced by a Tunnel.
p006-u013: Adjusted the overall layout of the Operator Room.
p006-u015: Added the High Point, Hangar Placement Zone, and Workbench.
p006-u017: Removed the Flight Zone and Wireless Charging Device Placement Zone.
p006-u018: This manual presents only some key rule changes. For complete rule details and final enforcement standards, refer to the official Rules Manual to be published later.

p011-u020: The Aerial Robot may launch from the Hangar and perform diverse attack and reconnaissance tasks on the battlefield.
p012-u002: Damage the opposing Outpost and Base Armor Modules by direct impact.
p012-u004: Intercept by actively colliding with and changing the flight paths of opposing Darts and projectiles.
p012-u006: Hover to gather information, then return to the Hangar and transmit it for further use by systems such as the Radar.
p012-u008: The Aerial Robot must meet the following requirements:
p012-u010: The Aerial Robot must be capable of hovering continuously for at least 10 seconds.
p012-u012: A fully enclosing propeller guard must be installed around the Aerial Robot. The propellers and body must not be exposed. When the Aerial Robot collides with an Armor Module at any angle and a certain horizontal speed, the guard must effectively prevent the propellers from contacting the Armor Module.
p012-u014: The Aerial Robot’s propellers must be made of flexible material.
p012-u016: The Aerial Robot must have a Remote Controller/receiver for emergency propeller shutdown and must have a safety officer.

p012-u040: The Hangar must meet the following requirements:

p013-u030: The Hangar may provide initial propulsion to the Aerial Robot, but the direction must be within a 15° cone around the Hangar’s vertical normal.
p013-u032: The Custom Terminal (formerly the Custom Controller and Custom Client) is a multipurpose device built by the team. It monitors robot motion and status, controls robot actions, receives match-related information and robot video from the Referee System Game Engine Server, and can send competition-specific interactive commands to that server to expand human-machine interaction.
p013-u033: A typical Custom Terminal may consist of a display, a computing platform (including memory, controller, and processor), and input devices. It may also be integrated into one device, such as a handheld tablet with an Ethernet port.
p013-u034: Example: A team builds a Custom Terminal that receives robot video and displays it on a custom screen with a custom UI overlaid through a nonofficial link, while a paired controller operates the robot. The team can therefore complete a match without using the official Referee System Operator End or a Remote Controller.
p014-u000: All Custom Terminals in the Operator Room may be connected to and communicate with one another by wire. A Custom Terminal may also connect to the Game Engine Server through the RJ45 port provided in the Operator Room and send and receive related content.
p014-u001: A Custom Terminal may receive match information displayed on the Referee System Operator End and available to its team, such as both teams’ HP, its team’s economy, remaining match time, and announcements of key match events.
p014-u002: A Custom Terminal may send the Referee System match commands supported by the Operator End, such as selecting a Performance System before the match, exchanging for permitted Projectile Allowance during a match, and intervening in Sentry actions.

p014-u025: The Custom Terminal must not use wireless transmitters or receivers.
p015-u002: The High Point is in the Base Zone. Three steps connect the trapezoidal high ground to the High Point, and robots may climb them to enter it.
p015-u006: All allied robots may occupy their team’s High Point Buff Point.
p015-u007: If a team’s High Point Buff Point is occupied by one of its robots, that robot receives a 50% defense Buff and may exchange non-remotely for permitted Projectile Allowance.
p015-u009: The former Launch Ramp is replaced by a Tunnel in the Highway Zone. Robots may pass through or over the Tunnel to reach the opposing half of the battlefield quickly.
p016-u002: The two types of buffs differ according to the type and sequence of Field Interaction Module cards detected while passing through the Tunnel:
p016-u013: A robot must detect each Field Interaction Module card in the Tunnel in sequence within 3 seconds, without detecting any other type of Field Interaction Module card along the way, to obtain the above Buff.
p016-u015: The Supply Zone includes the Resource Zone, Supply Zone Buff Point, and Workbench. It is an important area for robots to restore HP, replenish Projectile Allowance, obtain Energy Units, and assemble the modular 42mm launching mechanism.
p017-u001: The Workbench is in the Supply Zone. Robots may pick up and assemble the modular 42mm launching mechanism there.
p018-u001: The Hangar Placement Zone is in the center of the battlefield and is divided between the Red and Blue sides. Each side may install its Hangar only in its own Hangar Placement Zone.

p018-u005: The Operator Room is near the perimeter of the battlefield and is where Operators stay during matches. Each Operator desk is 120 cm long and 75 cm wide and is equipped with the corresponding number of computers. Each computer has a monitor, mouse, keyboard, Camera Video Transmitter Module (Receiver) and its stand, one 1GbE (RJ45) port, wired headphones, and other official equipment.
